title: Economies of scale and the equity-efficiency trade-off: Evidence from a piped water network in rural Bangladesh
abstract: arXiv:2611.08031v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Policymakers who set prices for public infrastructure often anticipate an equity-efficiency trade-off: while higher prices could increase revenues from fee-paying users, helping to offset costs, they may reduce take-up among the poor. But this trade-off is fundamentally altered in the presence of economies of scale, which are common in infrastructure networks. We elicit willingness to pay for a household-level piped drinking water connection in rural Bangladesh, where truthful revelation of preferences is incentivized by the opportunity to connect to a new pipeline network that we construct, and we use project cost data to measure economies of scale. Combining the two, we show that the cost-effectiveness-maximizing price---that which minimizes the cost per connected household---is zero. translated_title: 规模经济与公平-效率权衡：来自孟加拉国农村管道供水网络的证据
translated_abstract: 为公共基础设施定价的政策制定者通常会预期存在公平与效率之间的权衡：较高的价格可以增加付费用户带来的收入、有助于弥补成本，但可能会降低贫困人口的接入意愿。然而，在存在规模经济的情况下——这在基础设施网络中十分常见——这种权衡会发生根本性改变。我们针对孟加拉国农村的入户管道饮用水接入服务引导出支付意愿，其中通过接入我们新建管道网络的机会来激励受访者真实披露其偏好，并利用项目成本数据来衡量规模经济。将两者结合，我们证明了成本效益最大化价格——即使每户接入成本最小化的价格——为零。规模经济效应远超用户收费所带来的收入。更一般地，零价格实现成本效益最大化所需的两个条件……
tldr: 该研究利用在孟加拉国农村新建管道供水网络并激励式引导支付意愿的数据，证明由于规模经济效应远超用户收费收入，使每户接入成本最小化的最优定价为零。
en_tdlr: Using a newly constructed piped water network in rural Bangladesh with incentivized willingness-to-pay elicitation, this study shows that economies of scale strongly dominate user-fee revenues, so the cost-effectiveness-maximizing price is zero.
